title: Finite reduction and the canonical pullback square
statement: Let gprime: Xprime -> X, fprime: Xprime -> Yprime, f: X -> Y and g: Yprime -> Y form the chosen Cartesian square of def-weil-pbc-four-corners. Let d be its pro-etale adic coefficient datum, R_T the completed coefficient sheaf and P_(T,n) its quotient at exponent n+1. Put F_T = - tensor^L_(R_T) P_(T,n). For h: U -> V let delta_h: F_U composed with Lh_R^* -> Lh_P^* composed with F_V be the specified coefficient comparison of def-weil-pbc-four-corners. Let theta_R compare the pullback path Y -> Yprime -> Xprime with Y -> X -> Xprime, and theta_P the corresponding quotient-coefficient paths, as in def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange. For every M in D(Y,R_Y), F_Xprime(theta_R,M) followed by delta_gprime,LfM and Lgprime_P^*(delta_f,M) equals delta_fprime,LgM followed by Lfprime_P^*(delta_g,M) and theta_P,F_YM. No properness, completion condition on M, or etale-origin hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Take a flat-term K-flat resolution of M. Pullback along either leg preserves these properties. The characterizations of fourCornerReductionPullback and the canonical geometric composition identify their components on this representative with the localized ordinary coefficient and geometric comparisons.

The ordinary coefficient comparison is the conjugate of the identity on restriction/direct-image sections under the tensor-unit adjunctions. The geometric composition is the conjugate of fibre-product pasting. The two composite right-adjoint comparisons are equal on every section: each transports along the same pasting isomorphism and retains the same quotient scalar action. The coefficient projection compatibility identifies the actions. Conjugation, or evaluation on local balanced tensors, gives equality of the ordinary left-adjoint composites. On a local tensor both maps pull back its module section and multiply its quotient scalars in the same order; balancing and sheafification give equality on the whole module.

Apply the ordinary equality degreewise and localize. Use the normalization equations and invertibility of their factorization maps to cancel them, obtaining compatibility with each geometric composition. Naturality transports this equality across the resolution isomorphism to all derived M. Finally, the equality of the two composite scheme morphisms and their coefficient identifications transports the same single-morphism reduction comparison along equal sigma indices. Cancel the two composition isomorphisms to obtain the displayed pullback square equality.
